html:
The Cubeo, or Kubéwa, are a people of the Vaupés and Cuduyarí rivers in southeastern Colombia, with some villages across the border in Brazil. They speak one of the Tucanoan languages, and some of their clans are thought to have spoken an Arawakan language long ago.

They live in riverside villages, grow bitter manioc and fish. They are known for their mourning ceremonies, in which dancers wear bark cloth masks that stand for spirits and animals. Rubber traders in the early 1900s and then Catholic and Protestant missions changed their lives deeply. Neighbours: Yurutí and Wanano.
